default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1268.title: Noise-regime move fade
E-1268.hypothesis: When intrabar (Parkinson) variance far exceeds close-to-close variance, price is bouncing inside bars between quoters; a 5-minute move of 1.5 sigma in that regime is liquidity noise, so fade it.

E-1269.title: Equal-low / equal-high double test
E-1269.hypothesis: A second probe into the same low (high) after leaving it shows the same resting demand (supply) defending the level; buy the bullish bar at the retest, sell the bearish bar at an equal high.

E-1270.title: Floor-pivot S1/R1 rejection
E-1270.hypothesis: Floor-trader pivot levels from yesterday's H/L/C are watched by many discretionary traders; a poke beyond the level that closes back is absorbed by resting orders, so fade it.

E-1271.title: Relative-to-usual-path follow
E-1271.hypothesis: Today's move since the open compared with the average path of the same clock minute over recent sessions isolates unusual strength; when it exceeds the typical size, fresh flow is winning and continues.

E-1272.title: Anchored-VWAP support test
E-1272.hypothesis: VWAP anchored at the session low (high) is the average cost of everyone who bought (sold) since the turn; a dip to it that closes back above (below) is where those holders defend, so follow the turn.

E-1273.title: Choppiness range-edge fade
E-1273.hypothesis: A high choppiness index means the window is a sideways range; a bar turning back at the bottom (top) of that range is a range-trader's entry back toward the middle.

E-1274.title: Prior-close-location EMA turn
E-1274.hypothesis: Yesterday closing in the top (bottom) of its range leaves carried positions with the same bias; an intraday close back over (under) the short EMA is the dip-buyer's entry in that direction.

E-1275.title: Impulse flag break
E-1275.hypothesis: After an outsized bar, a few narrow bars held in its upper (lower) half show profit-taking without give-back; the close beyond the flag releases the next leg.

E-1276.title: Average-daily-range budget breach
E-1276.hypothesis: Moves from the open of a fraction of the 20-session average daily range show a day with above-normal participation; stops and chasers beyond that distance keep the push going.

E-1277.title: Impulse-bar midpoint retest
E-1277.hypothesis: A big bar closing in its top (bottom) third, followed by a pullback to its midpoint that holds and closes back above (below), shows the impulse buyers (sellers) defending half the bar; follow the impulse.
